title: Mekedatu & Dabbaguli ADV Circuit
tagline: Bengaluru → Bidadi thatte idli → Kanakapura → Chunchi Falls → Sangama (Kaveri–Arkavathy confluence) → a dirt trail to the Dabbaguli riverside on the Tamil Nadu border → home via Anekal. A one-day ADV loop, skipping the highways.
summary: A one-day adventure loop around south-west Bengaluru that skips the highways for backroads and forest. Breakfast at Bidadi, down the Kanakapura road to Chunchi Falls and the Sangama confluence and the Mekedatu gorge, then east through Kodihalli to a rocky, muddy trail into the Cauvery forest that ends at the raw riverbank at Dabbaguli. The return swings east along the Tamil Nadu border and comes back into the city via Anekal.

segments.note: Out of the city early; stop at Bidadi for thatte idli.
Quiet cross-country road that skips the highway.
Fast, wide stretch into Kanakapura. Last reliable fuel for a while.
Winding road south through scrub and hills. Detour to Chunchi Falls on the way.
Short, twisty run down to the confluence.

segments.road: Back north, then east via village roads
segments.note: Retrace towards Kanakapura, then cut east to Kodihalli.
Village roads, then about 10 km of rocky, muddy dirt trail down to the river. The same trail brings you back out.
Back up the trail, then backroads along the Karnataka–Tamil Nadu border to Anekal.
Back into the city from the south-east.

highlights: Thatte idli at Bidadi for breakfast
Chunchi Falls, spilling down a rock face in dozens of streams
Sangama, where the Arkavathy joins the Kaveri, and the Mekedatu gorge downstream
About 20 km of dirt trail (in and out) through the Cauvery forest
The raw, undeveloped riverbank at Dabbaguli
Whole loop avoids the big highways once you're past Bidadi

offroad.summary: Mostly tarmac, with a proper dirt section: about 10 km each way of rocky, muddy trail to Dabbaguli.
notes: Loose rock and ruts on the forest trail; stand on the pegs and keep momentum
Turns to mud after rain; road-biased tyres will struggle in the wet
Ride it with at least one other bike; there's little phone signal or help on the trail
Adventure bikes and scramblers are ideal; skip it on a low-slung road bike

timings: Dabbaguli: listed open 8 AM – 5 PM, two-wheeler entry about ₹30
Sangama: public buses to Mekedatu stop by about 5:30 PM
Fuel up at Kanakapura; nothing reliable between there and Anekal
Plan to be out of the forest well before dark
cautions: Do not enter the river at Dabbaguli: it has wild crocodiles
Rocks at Sangama and Mekedatu are steep and slippery, and currents are dangerous, especially after the monsoon
Wildlife sanctuary area: watch for elephants and other animals on the trail
Carry water, a puncture kit and a tow strap; the trail is remote
